On iPhone: the first tap of a speaker icon may prompt for audio. After that, all pronunciations work normally.

Italian B1 · citizenship exam

Study Master

2256 words in 77 semantic sections, plus a verb reference. Every word appears exactly once.

Read one section at a time, not the whole list. Each section is a small field of meaning, so the words you already know act as hooks for the ones beside them.

Click any word to open an example sentence with its translation. The most common words (tiers 1 and 2) carry two examples. Click again to close; several can stay open at once.

Context is a hint in plain English, never a definition, and blank when the translation already says everything. Synonyms are at most two, always words found elsewhere in this list.

Printing: Cmd+P → Save as PDF. Set to A4 landscape. Every example opens automatically on paper.

Section B — Tier 2 irregular verbs

Regular in the present tense; it is the past participle that has to be learned. — 20 verbs

Section B — Tier 2 irregular verbs
VerbEnglishPast tense (io)Note
nascereto be bornsono nato/aAlways with essere; the participle agrees with the person.
prendereto take, to catchho presoSame participle shape in scendere, spendere, offendere.
mettereto putho messoCompounds follow: promettere, permettere, trasmettere.
aprireto openho apertoPresent tense is regular; only the participle surprises you.
chiudereto closeho chiusoSame shape as decidere and the verb for 'to lose'.
leggereto readho lettoShort participle from a long verb; also in eleggere.
scrivereto writeho scrittoCompounds follow: descrivere, iscriversi.
chiedereto askho chiestoAsk someone for something takes a before the person.
rispondereto answerho rispostoAnswer someone takes a before the person.
decidereto decideho decisoDecide to do something takes di before the plain verb.
perdereto lose, to missho persoA longer regular form also exists but is rarer.
vincereto winho vintoSame shape in convincere.
offrireto offer, to buy a drinkho offertoSame participle shape as the verb for 'to suffer'.
correreto runho corsoTakes essere when a destination follows.
vivereto liveho vissutoEssere is also possible and is common in the north.
conoscereto know a personho conosciutoIn the past tense it shifts to 'met for the first time'.
tradurreto translateho tradottoBehaves like a longer hidden verb, as in produrre.
succedereto happenè successoThird person only; the thing that happened is the subject.
piacereto like, to pleasemi è piaciutoThe thing liked is the subject, so the participle agrees with it.
cadereto fallsono caduto/aTakes essere; the future doubles the d.

Section D — Verbs whose past tense uses essere

With these, the ending agrees with who is speaking. Mined from this list. — 99 verbs

Movement from A to B (14)

Where the verb takes you somewhere, or away from it.

andare, venire, arrivare, partire, tornare, ritornare, entrare, uscire, salire, scendere, cadere, correre, volare, emigrare

Change of state (19)

Becoming something you were not before.

nascere, morire, crescere, diventare, cambiare, aumentare, diminuire, migliorare, guarire, scadere, finire, cominciare, iniziare, riuscire, nevicare, piovere, esistere, risultare, succedere

Staying put (7)

The opposite of movement — still essere.

essere, stare, restare, rimanere, durare, costare, vivere

Reflexive verbs (49)

Every single one, without exception.

accomodarsi, addormentarsi, alzarsi, ammalarsi, annoiarsi, arrabbiarsi, asciugarsi, bagnarsi, bruciarsi, calmarsi, candidarsi, chiamarsi, comportarsi, connettersi, dimenticarsi, dimettersi, diplomarsi, divertirsi, ferirsi, fermarsi, incontrarsi, innamorarsi, interessarsi, iscriversi, laurearsi, lavarsi, mettersi, muoversi, occuparsi, piegarsi, preoccuparsi, ricordarsi, rilassarsi, riposarsi, rompersi, sbagliarsi, sdraiarsi, sedersi, sentirsi, separarsi, spogliarsi, sposarsi, stendersi, svegliarsi, trasferirsi, trovarsi, ubriacarsi, vedersi, vestirsi

Impersonal and backwards verbs (8)

Weather, seeming, and verbs whose subject is the thing.

piacere, dispiacere, mancare, sembrare, servire, importare, bisognare, dipendere

Others in this list (2)

Also take the same auxiliary.

appartenere, crepare

Section E — Verbs with an obligatory preposition

The little word is not optional: leaving it out is the commonest B1 mistake. — 54 verbs

a + plain verb

The second verb keeps its dictionary form.

cominciare — to start doing
iniziare — to begin doing
continuare — to keep doing
imparare — to learn to do
insegnare — to teach someone to do
aiutare — to help someone do
riuscire — to manage to do

andare — to go and do
venire — to come and do
mettersi — to set about doing
invitare — to invite someone to do

di + plain verb

By far the commonest pattern after an opinion verb.

finire — to finish doing
smettere — to stop doing
cercare — to try to do
decidere — to decide to do
dimenticare — to forget to do
ricordarsi — to remember to do
sperare — to hope to do
pensare — to plan to do

chiedere — to ask to do

promettere — to promise to do
permettere — to allow someone to do
evitare — to avoid doing
consigliare — to advise someone to do
proporre — to suggest doing

The object needs the little word a in front of it.

rispondere — to answer someone
chiedere — to ask someone
dire — to say to someone

mandare — to send to someone
dare — to give to someone

pensare — to think about something
credere — to believe in something
giocare — to play a sport or game
partecipare — to take part in
servire — to be useful for something
assistere — to attend an event

di + person or thing

Often where English uses about, of, or nothing at all.

parlare — to talk about something
occuparsi — to deal with something
trattare — to be about a subject
ricordarsi — to remember something
dimenticarsi — to forget something
innamorarsi — to fall in love with
preoccuparsi — to worry about something
interessarsi — to be interested in
accorgersi — to notice something
fidarsi — to trust someone
avere paura — to be afraid of
avere bisogno — to need
